question.problem: If a curve $C$ is given by $y=(2x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡x,$ calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=1$ is{{field-1}}.

current_example.problem: If a curve $\mathcal C$ is given by $y=e^x\sin x,$ calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=\dfrac \pi 2.$
current_example.worked_solution:
We differentiate using the product rule. Let $u(x) = e^x$ and $v(x)=\sin{x}.$ Then, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = e^x,\qquad \dfrac{\textrm d v}{\textrm d x} = \cos x.
$$

Applying the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{x}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & ={e}^{x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=\dfrac\pi 2$ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=\pi /2} & ={e}^{\pi /2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})) \\  & ={e}^{\pi /2}(0+1) \\  & ={e}^{\pi /2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $e^{\pi/2}.$
